sanskrit: tataḥ sutumulaṃ yuddhaṃ gandharvāṇāṃ tarasvinām babhūva bhīmavegānāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca bhārata
english: Then a most tumultuous battle arose between the swift Gandharvas of terrible speed and the Pandavas, O Bharata.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato divyāstrasaṃpannā gandharvā hemamālinaḥ visṛjantaḥ śarān dīptān samantāt paryavārayan
english: Vaishampayana said: Then the Gandharvas, equipped with divine weapons and wearing golden garlands, released blazing arrows and surrounded them from all sides.

sanskrit: catvāraḥ pāṇḍavā vīrā gandharvāś ca sahasraśaḥ raṇe saṃnyapatan rājaṃs tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: The four heroic Pandavas and the Gandharvas by the thousands clashed in battle, O king — it was truly a wondrous sight.

sanskrit: yathā karṇasya ca ratho dhārtarāṣṭrasya cobhayoḥ gandharvaiḥ śataśaś chinnau tathā teṣāṃ pracakrire
english: Just as the chariots of Karna and Duryodhana had both been shattered by the Gandharvas in hundreds of pieces, so they now did the same to those others.

sanskrit: tān samāpatato rājan gandharvāñ śataśo raṇe pratyagṛhṇan naravyāghrāḥ śaravarṣair anekaśaḥ
english: Those tiger-like men received those hundreds of Gandharvas charging in battle, O king, with showers of arrows manifold.

sanskrit: avakīryamāṇāḥ khagamāḥ śaravarṣaiḥ samantataḥ na śekuḥ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ samīpe parivartitum
english: The sky-travellers, pelted with showers of arrows from all sides, could not remain near the sons of Pandu.

sanskrit: abhikruddhān abhiprekṣya gandharvān arjunas tadā lakṣayitvātha divyāni mahāstrāṇy upacakrame
english: Seeing the Gandharvas enraged and bearing down on him, Arjuna then took aim and prepared to employ the great divine weapons.

sanskrit: sahasrāṇāṃ sahasraṃ sa prāhiṇod yamasādanam āgneyenārjunaḥ saṃkhye gandharvāṇāṃ balotkaṭaḥ
english: With the fire-weapon (Agneya), the mighty Arjuna sent a thousand thousands of those Gandharvas to the abode of Yama in battle.

sanskrit: tathā bhīmo maheṣvāsaḥ saṃyuge balināṃ varaḥ gandharvāñ śataśo rājañ jaghāna niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Likewise Bhima, the great archer, foremost among the strong in battle, slew hundreds of Gandharvas, O king, with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: mādrīputrāv api tathā yudhyamānau balotkaṭau parigṛhyāgrato rājañ jaghnatuḥ śataśaḥ parān
english: The two sons of Madri also, those mighty warriors fighting fiercely, pressing forward, O king, slew hundreds of enemies.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānā gandharvā divyair astrair mahātmabhiḥ utpetuḥ kham upādāya dhṛtarāṣṭrasutāṃs tataḥ
english: Those Gandharvas, being slaughtered by the divine weapons of those great-souled ones, then flew up into the sky, taking the sons of Dhritarashtra with them.

sanskrit: tān utpatiṣṇūn buddhvā tu kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ mahatā śarajālena samantāt paryavārayat
english: Perceiving them as they attempted to fly upward, the son of Kunti, Dhananjaya, surrounded them on all sides with a great net of arrows.

sanskrit: te baddhāḥ śarajālena śakuntā iva pañjare vavarṣur arjunaṃ krodhād gadāśaktyṛṣṭivṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: Caught in that net of arrows like birds in a cage, they showered Arjuna in anger with a rain of maces, javelins, and iron bolts.

sanskrit: gadāśaktyasivṛṣṭīs tā nihatya sa mahāstravit gātrāṇi cāhanad bhallair gandharvāṇāṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Destroying those volleys of maces, javelins, and swords, that master of great weapons, Dhananjaya, struck the bodies of the Gandharvas with broad-headed arrows.

sanskrit: śirobhiḥ prapatadbhiś ca caraṇair bāhubhis tathā aśmavṛṣṭir ivābhāti pareṣām abhavad bhayam
english: With heads, feet, and arms raining down, it appeared like a shower of stones, and great fear arose among the enemies.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānā gandharvāḥ pāṇḍavena mahātmanā bhūmiṣṭham antarikṣasthāḥ śaravarṣair avākiran
english: Those Gandharvas being slaughtered by that great-souled Pandava, though stationed in the sky, showered down arrows upon those on the ground.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu śaravarṣāṇi savyasācī paraṃtapaḥ astraiḥ saṃvārya tejasvī gandharvān pratyavidhyata
english: But Savyasachin, the scorcher of foes, that resplendent one, warded off their showers of arrows with his own weapons and pierced the Gandharvas in return.

sanskrit: sthūṇākarṇendrajālaṃ ca sauraṃ cāpi tathārjunaḥ āgneyaṃ cāpi saumyaṃ ca sasarja kurunandanaḥ
english: Arjuna, the joy of the Kurus, also deployed the Sthunakarna, the Indrajala, the Saura, the Agneya, and the Saumya weapons.

sanskrit: te dahyamānā gandharvāḥ kuntīputrasya sāyakaiḥ daiteyā iva śakreṇa viṣādam agaman param
english: Those Gandharvas, scorched by the arrows of the son of Kunti, fell into utter despair, like the Daityas struck down by Indra.

sanskrit: ūrdhvam ākramamāṇāś ca śarajālena vāritāḥ visarpamāṇā bhallaiś ca vāryante savyasācinā
english: Attempting to ascend upward they were blocked by the net of arrows; trying to scatter they were checked by Savyasachin's broad-headed shafts.

sanskrit: gandharvāṃs trāsitān dṛṣṭvā kuntīputreṇa dhīmatā citraseno gadāṃ gṛhya savyasācinam ādravat
english: Seeing the Gandharvas terrified by the wise son of Kunti, Chitrasena seized a mace and rushed at Savyasachin.

sanskrit: tasyābhipatatas tūrṇaṃ gadāhastasya saṃyuge gadāṃ sarvāyasīṃ pārthaḥ śaraiś ciccheda saptadhā
english: As he came rushing swiftly, mace in hand, in that battle, the son of Pritha cut that all-iron mace into seven pieces with his arrows.

sanskrit: sa gadāṃ bahudhā dṛṣṭvā kṛttāṃ bāṇais tarasvinā saṃvṛtya vidyayātmānaṃ yodhayām āsa pāṇḍavam astrāṇi tasya divyāni yodhayām āsa khe sthitaḥ
english: Seeing his mace cut into many pieces by that swift archer, he concealed himself with his magic art and fought the Pandava, deploying his divine weapons while standing in the sky.

sanskrit: gandharvarājo balavān māyayāntarhitas tadā antarhitaṃ samālakṣya praharantam athārjunaḥ tāḍayām āsa khacarair divyāstrapratimantritaiḥ
english: The mighty king of the Gandharvas then made himself invisible through illusion; perceiving the invisible one striking at him, Arjuna struck back with sky-travelling arrows empowered with divine weapon-mantras.

sanskrit: antardhānavadhaṃ cāsya cakre kruddho 'rjunas tadā śabdavedhyam upāśritya bahurūpo dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: The enraged Arjuna then attempted to slay the invisible one, and Dhananjaya, taking many forms, relied upon the technique of piercing by sound.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamānas tair astrair arjunena mahātmanā athāsya darśayām āsa tadātmānaṃ priyaḥ sakhā
english: As he was being struck by those weapons of the great-souled Arjuna, his dear friend then revealed himself to him.

sanskrit: citrasenam athālakṣya sakhāyaṃ yudhi durbalam saṃjahārāstram atha tat prasṛṣṭaṃ pāṇḍavarṣabhaḥ
english: Recognizing Chitrasena as his friend, weakened in battle, the bull among Pandavas then withdrew that weapon already released.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavāḥ sarve saṃhṛtāstraṃ dhanaṃjayam saṃjahruḥ pradrutān aśvāñ śaravegān dhanūṃṣi ca
english: Seeing Dhananjaya withdraw his weapon, all the Pandavas likewise reined in their galloping horses, checked the speed of their arrows, and lowered their bows.

sanskrit: citrasenaś ca bhīmaś ca savyasācī yamāv api pṛṣṭvā kauśalam anyonyaṃ ratheṣv evāvatasthire
english: Chitrasena, Bhima, Savyasachin, and the twin sons of Madri, having inquired of each other's well-being, all remained in their chariots.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato 'rjunaś citrasenaṃ prahasann idam abravīt madhye gandharvasainyānāṃ maheṣvāso mahādyutiḥ
english: Vaishampayana said: Then Arjuna, that great archer of great splendor, smiling, spoke these words to Chitrasena in the midst of the Gandharva army.

sanskrit: kiṃ te vyavasitaṃ vīra kauravāṇāṃ vinigrahe kimarthaṃ ca sadāro 'yaṃ nigṛhītaḥ suyodhanaḥ
english: "What was your purpose, O hero, in restraining the Kauravas? And for what reason has this Suyodhana been seized along with his wives?"

sanskrit: citrasena uvāca vidito 'yam abhiprāyas tatrasthena mahātmanā duryodhanasya pāpasya karṇasya ca dhanaṃjaya
english: Chitrasena said: "This intention of the wicked Duryodhana and of Karna was known to the great-souled one who dwells there, O Dhananjaya.

sanskrit: vanasthān bhavato jñātvā kliśyamānān anarhavat ime 'vahasituṃ prāptā draupadīṃ ca yaśasvinīm
english: Knowing you to be dwelling in the forest and suffering hardship undeservedly, these ones came to mock you and the illustrious Draupadi.

sanskrit: jñātvā cikīrṣitaṃ caiṣāṃ mām uvāca sureśvaraḥ gaccha duryodhanaṃ baddhvā sāmātyaṃ tvam ihānaya
english: Knowing what they intended to do, the lord of the gods spoke to me: 'Go, bind Duryodhana together with his ministers and bring them here.'

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayaś ca te rakṣyaḥ saha bhrātṛbhir āhave sa hi priyaḥ sakhā tubhyaṃ śiṣyaś ca tava pāṇḍavaḥ
english: 'And Dhananjaya must be protected in battle along with his brothers, for that Pandava is your dear friend and also your pupil.'

sanskrit: vacanād devarājasya tato 'smīhāgato drutam ayaṃ durātmā baddhaś ca gamiṣyāmi surālayam
english: "By the command of the king of the gods I came here swiftly; this evil one is now bound, and I shall take him to the abode of the gods."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca utsṛjyatāṃ citrasena bhrātāsmākaṃ suyodhanaḥ dharmarājasya saṃdeśān mama ced icchasi priyam
english: Arjuna said: "Release him, Chitrasena — Suyodhana is our brother. If you wish to please me, do so at the command of Dharmaraja."

sanskrit: citrasena uvāca pāpo 'yaṃ nityasaṃduṣṭo na vimokṣaṇam arhati pralabdhā dharmarājasya kṛṣṇāyāś ca dhanaṃjaya
english: Chitrasena said: "This sinful one, ever corrupt, does not deserve to be released — he has cheated Dharmaraja and Krishna (Draupadi), O Dhananjaya.

sanskrit: nedaṃ cikīrṣitaṃ tasya kuntīputro mahāvrataḥ jānāti dharmarājo hi śrutvā kuru yathecchasi
english: "The son of Kunti, Dharmaraja, that one of great vows, does not know what this one intended to do — inform him, and then do as you wish."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca te sarva eva rājānam abhijagmur yudhiṣṭhiram abhigamya ca tat sarvaṃ śaśaṃsus tasya duṣkṛtam
english: Vaishampayana said: They all then went to king Yudhishthira, and having approached him, they reported in full all of his evil deeds.

sanskrit: ajātaśatrus tac chrutvā gandharvasya vacas tadā mokṣayām āsa tān sarvān gandharvān praśaśaṃsa ca
english: Ajatashatru, having heard those words of the Gandharva, then caused them all to be released and praised the Gandharvas.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā bhavadbhir balibhiḥ śaktaiḥ sarvair na hiṃsitaḥ durvṛtto dhārtarāṣṭro 'yaṃ sāmātyajñātibāndhavaḥ
english: "By good fortune this ill-behaved son of Dhritarashtra, together with his ministers, kinsmen, and relatives, was not slain by you, who are all powerful and capable.

sanskrit: upakāro mahāṃs tāta kṛto 'yaṃ mama khecarāḥ kulaṃ na paribhūtaṃ me mokṣeṇāsya durātmanaḥ
english: "A great service has been done for me, O sky-travellers, my dear ones — by releasing this wicked one, our family has not been put to shame.

sanskrit: ājñāpayadhvam iṣṭāni prīyāmo darśanena vaḥ prāpya sarvān abhiprāyāṃs tato vrajata māciram
english: "Command whatever you desire; we are pleased by your sight. Having received all that you wish, then depart without delay."

sanskrit: anujñātās tu gandharvāḥ pāṇḍuputreṇa dhīmatā sahāpsarobhiḥ saṃhṛṣṭāś citrasenamukhā yayuḥ
english: Dismissed by the wise son of Pandu, the Gandharvas, led by Chitrasena, departed joyfully together with the Apsaras.

sanskrit: devarāḍ api gandharvān mṛtāṃs tān samajīvayat divyenāmṛtavarṣeṇa ye hatāḥ kauravair yudhi
english: The king of the gods also revived those Gandharvas who had been slain in battle by the Kauravas, with a divine shower of nectar.

sanskrit: jñātīṃs tān avamucyātha rājadārāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ kṛtvā ca duṣkaraṃ karma prītiyuktāś ca pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Having thus freed those kinsmen and all the royal wives, and having accomplished that difficult feat, the Pandavas were filled with joy.

sanskrit: sastrīkumāraiḥ kurubhiḥ pūjyamānā mahārathāḥ babhrājire mahātmānaḥ kurumadhye yathāgnayaḥ
english: Honored by the Kuru men, women, and children, those great chariot-warriors, those great-souled ones, shone in the midst of the Kurus like fires.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaṃ mucya bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaṃ tadā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ sapraṇayam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then, having freed Duryodhana together with his brothers, Yudhishthira spoke these affectionate words:

sanskrit: mā sma tāta punaḥ kārṣīr īdṛśaṃ sāhasaṃ kva cit na hi sāhasakartāraḥ sukham edhanti bhārata
english: "Do not commit such a rash act again anywhere, my dear one — for those who act rashly do not prosper in happiness, O Bharata.

sanskrit: svastimān sahitaḥ sarvair bhrātṛbhiḥ kurunandana gṛhān vraja yathākāmaṃ vaimanasyaṃ ca mā kṛthāḥ
english: "Go home safely together with all your brothers, O joy of the Kurus, as you please — and do not harbor grief in your heart."

sanskrit: pāṇḍavenābhyanujñāto rājā duryodhanas tadā vidīryamāṇo vrīḍena jagāma nagaraṃ prati
english: Thus dismissed by the Pandava, king Duryodhana then, splitting apart with shame, went toward his city.

sanskrit: tasmin gate kauraveye kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito vīraḥ pūjyamāno dvijātibhiḥ
english: After that Kaurava had gone, the heroic son of Kunti, Yudhishthira, together with his brothers, honored by the twice-born,

sanskrit: tapodhanaiś ca taiḥ sarvair vṛtaḥ śakra ivāmaraiḥ vane dvaitavane tasmin vijahāra mudā yutaḥ
english: surrounded by all those ascetics rich in spiritual power, like Indra among the immortals, sported joyfully in that Dvaita forest.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca śatrubhir jitabaddhasya pāṇḍavaiś ca mahātmabhiḥ mokṣitasya yudhā paścān mānasthasya durātmanaḥ
english: Janamejaya said: Of that evil one, conquered and captured by enemies and then freed in battle by the great-souled Pandavas, and yet still proud afterward —

sanskrit: katthanasyāvaliptasya garvitasya ca nityaśaḥ sadā ca pauruṣaudāryaiḥ pāṇḍavān avamanyataḥ
english: — of him who boasted and was arrogant and haughty always, and who always despised the Pandavas for their manly valor and generosity —

sanskrit: duryodhanasya pāpasya nityāhaṃkāravādinaḥ praveśo hāstinapure duṣkaraḥ pratibhāti me
english: — the entry of that sinful Duryodhana, that constant speaker of ego, into Hastinapura seems difficult to imagine to me.

sanskrit: tasya lajjānvitasyaiva śokavyākulacetasaḥ praveśaṃ vistareṇa tvaṃ vaiśaṃpāyana kīrtaya
english: Narrate in detail, O Vaishampayana, the entry of one so filled with shame, his mind overwhelmed with grief.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dharmarājanisṛṣṭas tu dhārtarāṣṭraḥ suyodhanaḥ lajjayādhomukhaḥ sīdann upāsarpat suduḥkhitaḥ
english: Vaishampayana said: Dismissed by Dharmaraja, that son of Dhritarashtra, Suyodhana, head bowed in shame, approached in sorrow, utterly wretched.

sanskrit: svapuraṃ prayayau rājā caturaṅgabalānugaḥ śokopahatayā buddhyā cintayānaḥ parābhavam
english: The king proceeded to his own city followed by his fourfold army, his mind struck by grief, brooding upon his defeat.

sanskrit: vimucya pathi yānāni deśe suyavasodake saṃniviṣṭaḥ śubhe ramye bhūmibhāge yathepsitam hastyaśvarathapādātaṃ yathāsthānaṃ nyaveśayat
english: Halting the vehicles along the way in a pleasant place with good pasture and water, he encamped on a beautiful and charming stretch of land as he wished, and stationed the elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry each in their proper place.

sanskrit: athopaviṣṭaṃ rājānaṃ paryaṅke jvalanaprabhe upaplutaṃ yathā somaṃ rāhuṇā rātrisaṃkṣaye upagamyābravīt karṇo duryodhanam idaṃ tadā
english: Then, as the king sat upon a couch brilliant as fire, afflicted like the moon seized by Rahu at the waning of night, Karna approached and spoke these words to Duryodhana:

sanskrit: diṣṭyā jīvasi gāndhāre diṣṭyā naḥ saṃgamaḥ punaḥ diṣṭyā tvayā jitāś caiva gandharvāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ
english: "By good fortune you live, O son of Gandhari! By good fortune we meet again! By good fortune you have conquered those shape-shifting Gandharvas!

sanskrit: diṣṭyā samagrān paśyāmi bhrātṝṃs te kurunandana vijigīṣūn raṇān muktān nirjitārīn mahārathān
english: "By good fortune I see all your brothers whole, O joy of the Kurus — those great chariot-warriors, eager for battle, freed, their enemies defeated.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tv abhidrutaḥ sarvair gandharvaiḥ paśyatas tava nāśaknuvaṃ sthāpayituṃ dīryamāṇāṃ svavāhinīm
english: "But I, attacked by all the Gandharvas as you watched, was unable to hold firm my own army as it was torn apart.

sanskrit: śarakṣatāṅgaś ca bhṛśaṃ vyapayāto 'bhipīḍitaḥ idaṃ tv atyadbhutaṃ manye yad yuṣmān iha bhārata
english: "Grievously wounded by arrows and utterly distressed I withdrew — but what I consider most extraordinary, O Bharata, is that you here —

sanskrit: ariṣṭān akṣatāṃś cāpi sadāradhanavāhanān vimuktān saṃprapaśyāmi tasmād yuddhād amānuṣāt
english: "— I see you freed from that superhuman battle, unharmed, unscathed, together with your wives, wealth, and vehicles.

sanskrit: naitasya kartā loke 'smin pumān vidyeta bhārata yatkṛtaṃ te mahārāja saha bhrātṛbhir āhave
english: "There could be found no man in this world, O Bharata, who could have done what you did, O great king, in that battle along with your brothers."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu karṇena rājā duryodhanas tadā uvācāvākśirā rājan bāṣpagadgadayā girā
english: Thus addressed by Karna, king Duryodhana then, head bowed low, O king, spoke in a voice choked with tears:

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca ajānatas te rādheya nābhyasūyāmy ahaṃ vacaḥ jānāsi tvaṃ jitāñ śatrūn gandharvāṃs tejasā mayā
english: Duryodhana said: "I do not resent your words spoken in ignorance, O son of Radha — you know that those Gandharva enemies were conquered by my valor.

sanskrit: āyodhitās tu gandharvāḥ suciraṃ sodarair mama mayā saha mahābāho kṛtaś cobhayataḥ kṣayaḥ
english: "The Gandharvas were fought for a long time by my brothers and me together, O mighty-armed one, and great losses were inflicted on both sides.

sanskrit: māyādhikās tv ayudhyanta yadā śūrā viyadgatāḥ tadā no nasamaṃ yuddham abhavat saha khecaraiḥ
english: "But when those heroic sky-travellers fought with superior magic from the air, then our battle with those sky-goers became unequal.

sanskrit: parājayaṃ ca prāptāḥ sma raṇe bandhanam eva ca sabhṛtyāmātyaputrāś ca sadāradhanavāhanāḥ uccair ākāśamārgeṇa hriyāmas taiḥ suduḥkhitāḥ
english: "We suffered defeat in battle and actual capture — I, along with my servants, ministers' sons, wives, wealth, and vehicles, were being carried off by them high along the aerial path, greatly distressed.

sanskrit: atha naḥ sainikāḥ ke cid amātyāś ca mahārathān upagamyābruvan dīnāḥ pāṇḍavāñ śaraṇapradān
english: "Then some of our soldiers and ministers, pitiful and helpless, approached those great chariot-warriors — the Pandavas — who grant refuge, and spoke to them.

sanskrit: eṣa duryodhano rājā dhārtarāṣṭraḥ sahānujaḥ sāmātyadāro hriyate gandharvair divam āsthitaiḥ
english: "'This is king Duryodhana, son of Dhritarashtra, along with his younger brothers — he is being carried off, together with his ministers and wives, by Gandharvas who have taken to the sky.'

sanskrit: taṃ mokṣayata bhadraṃ vaḥ sahadāraṃ narādhipam parāmarśo mā bhaviṣyat kurudāreṣu sarvaśaḥ
english: "'Free him, blessings upon you — free this lord of men together with his wives; let there be no insult whatsoever inflicted upon the Kuru women.'

sanskrit: evam ukte tu dharmātmā jyeṣṭhaḥ pāṇḍusutas tadā prasādya sodarān sarvān ājñāpayata mokṣaṇe
english: "When this was said, the righteous eldest son of Pandu, having appeased all his brothers, commanded them to effect the release.

sanskrit: athāgamya tam uddeśaṃ pāṇḍavāḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ sāntvapūrvam ayācanta śaktāḥ santo mahārathāḥ
english: "Then the Pandavas, those bulls among men, those capable and righteous great chariot-warriors, came to that place and first entreated them with conciliatory words.

sanskrit: yadā cāsmān na mumucur gandharvāḥ sāntvitā api tato 'rjunaś ca bhīmaś ca yamajau ca balotkaṭau mumucuḥ śaravarṣāṇi gandharvān pratyanekaśaḥ
english: "When the Gandharvas, even though appeased, did not release us, then Arjuna, Bhima, and the mighty twin sons of Madri released shower upon shower of arrows against the Gandharvas manifold times.

sanskrit: atha sarve raṇaṃ muktvā prayātāḥ khacarā divam asmān evābhikarṣanto dīnān muditamānasāḥ
english: "Then all those sky-travellers, abandoning the battle, departed for the sky, dragging us wretched ones along, their minds joyful —
